body:
MAINLINE-071 is filed. On an aluminum core the graphite route has no feasible shell. QUESTIONABLE. PROJECTION. No qualified hull safety factor.

Above Vc 2, CR-1457 governs by shear crimping and sets the knockdown to 1. No further knockdown is on that stress. 070's step sits near Vc 3.1 with crimping active, so gamma 1 matches the handbook. It is admissible with a named limit: not this film on CR-III, and not a closed 20 to 30 m sphere. DOI 10.2514/3.5568 and DOI 10.2514/3.1932 do not govern it.

The signed expansion is the HOPG catalogue value, -1.0e-6 per K, not the film. The interface coefficient becomes 24.6e-6. Every gamma-step case is infeasible. At 070's geometry the thermal margin is 0.536. Face density cannot release it. A core expansion of 12.2e-6 per K would, at this stiffness. The 25 psi screen must rise by 1.866, to 0.322 MPa, above the core's own W shear. Cure temperature is not in the interface stress.

The scarf screen is 10 MPa, an owner assumption, not a measured allowable. At the thermal boundary its margin is 2.89, and doubling it does not change the payload.

At the largest mismatch that is just feasible, R 20 optimistic still needs a face-density factor of 3.467 at concept and 3.137 at TRL 7, to 649 and 717 kg/m3. That core thickness is the search floor. Those factors are worse than 070's 1.248 and 1.126.
